title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page states, without proof, the standard lemma giving a presentation of a group extension from presentations of the kernel and the quotient. Let 1 → L → π̃ → π → 1 be exact. Take generators x_i (i∈I) of π with defining relations R_α(x)=1 (α∈A), and generators a_j (j∈J) of L with defining relations S_β(a)=1 (β∈B). Lift each x_i to some x̃_i in π̃. Then:
(1) Each lifted relator R_α(x̃) lies in L, so it equals some word M_α(a).
(2) Each conjugate x̃_i a_j x̃_i^{-1} lies in L, so it equals some word M_ij(a).
The lemma says that (1), (2) and (3) S_β(a)=1 form a presentation of π̃ on the generators (x̃_i), (a_j).
Proof sketch (not on the page): let G be the group so presented, with its obvious surjection onto π̃. Let N be the subgroup of G generated by the a_j.
- N ≅ L: the group presented by the S_β maps onto N, and the composite to L ⊂ π̃ is an isomorphism.
- N is normal in G. Relation (2) gives x̃_i N x̃_i^{-1} ⊆ N. The reverse inclusion x̃_i^{-1} N x̃_i ⊆ N follows by pulling back through the isomorphism N ≅ L.
- G/N is presented by the R_α, so G/N ≅ π.
- The five lemma then gives G ≅ π̃.
The NB treats the central case. If L is central in π̃, choose M_ij to be the empty word, so (2) becomes the commutation relations [x̃_i, a_j]=1. Marginal labels name the three families: the 'lifted' relations R_α of π, the 'conjugation' relations r(i,j), and the 'relations of L' S_β.
Purpose in the dossier: the next page extends the lemma to a homomorphism of groupoids T̃ → T that is surjective on π_0. There, lifted generating arrows and 'fibre arrows' (arrows projecting to identities) play the roles of x̃_i and a_j. This is clearly meant to present Teichmüller groupoids T̃ that are extensions of simpler ones. The central case fits extensions by central twists (e.g. boundary Dehn twists, or the central Z in braid/mapping-class extensions).
errors: No mathematical error. Only the forward conjugates x̃_i a_j x̃_i^{-1} are required; normality of the subgroup generated by the a_j in the presented group still follows, because that subgroup maps isomorphically onto L. So the statement is correct as written.
Minor slip of the pen: 'par aux générateurs' is presumably 'par rapport aux générateurs'.

ideas.what: Presentation of a group extension from presentations of kernel and quotient: lifted relators, conjugation relators, kernel relators
ideas.modern_name: Standard presentation of an extension (P. Hall's lemma / presentation of extensions; cf. D.L. Johnson, 'Presentations of Groups')
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Hall (1930s/1950s); folklore in combinatorial group theory

ideas.what: Central extension case: conjugation relations become commutators [x̃_i, a_j]=1
Planned extension to groupoids (next page): presenting T̃ from a presentation of T plus 'fibre arrows', for a groupoid map surjective on π_0
ideas.modern_name: Presentations of groupoid extensions / fibrations of groupoids (cf. R. Brown, P.J. Higgins)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook lemma (Hall's presentation of an extension) stated as a tool for presenting Teichmüller groupoids. Only the groupoid version on the next page shows intent, and that is also routine.
transcription_corrections: 'choisissons des mots en M_α et M_ij ... en des lettres a_j' should read 'choisissons des mots M_α et M_{ij} (α∈A, (i,j)∈I×J) en des lettres a_j'. The first 'en' is spurious; a crossed-out fragment precedes (i,j).
Final line: 'par aux générateurs' is likely an abbreviation of 'par rapport aux générateurs (x̃_i), (a_j)'.
Margin note at (1) reads roughly 'relations R_α de π "relevées"'; at (2) 'relations r(i,j) "de conjugaison"'; at (3) '"relations de L" des S_β'. This matches the transcription.
